title: Paris impressions, Kenny Clarke, Delaunay and Panassie
summary: Kind treatment in Paris contrasted with American racism; Panassie criticises his style.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So how did Paris and Europe hit you after having been living here all your life, and...?

Oh, it was just... The people in Paris were so nice that I couldn't hardly believe that they were sincere about being that nice. But they were. They were just nice people. And that I had never really seen too much, because all the shit that I went through when I was a kid and when I was coming up, like Oklahoma and Texas and New Mexico and Colorado and Wyoming and Montana and North Dakota and South Dakota and all that shit... It's horrible, you know, the way they treat Negroes. But I mean, that's the way the country was. What can you say? They treat 'em a little different now. Now they hang 'em. Ha-ha-ha...!
But not only the other culture there, but you ran into a thing where the people who were into the music were really...

Well, Bean had told me about a lot about Paris, so I knew what to expect when I got there. Of course, he was on the show, too, you know. I didn't see him that much when I was in Paris, but I know when we'd play... Well, when we were supposed to be on stage together, we were there together. He hung out with other people. But Kenny Clarke and I hung out mostly in Paris. He introduced me to Charles Delaunay and another guy, an old fellow that was a Dixieland buff...

Panassie. I met him over there. He was trying to tell me about "You don't play like you used to play." I had to tell him, "What difference does it make, as long as I'm playing?" He was talking about that old school, and man, I wasn't for that. I wasn't for that old school business at all.
Now, you played a Jazz festival there?
Yeah, we played that... We played in Paris for a week, and then we played a couple of one-nighters around Lyon and some other place, maybe Nice. But anyway,
it was very nice. I enjoyed being over there. The people were very nice. So were the girls.
So we stayed over there for maybe about twelve days, then came back here to New York, and went into Chicago -- the Argyle Lounge. Let's see, what happens after that...
